profile.reading:
Per Flexential's own individual facility page, this building (Flexential Tampa - North) is located at 8350 Parkedge Drive, Tampa, FL 33637. The operator publishes a footprint of 60166 square feet and 3 MW of critical load UPS capacity for this specific building, with published certifications and compliance attestations including PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, HIPAA, ISO 27001, SSAE 18. Duke Energy, a major Florida utility, announced a five-year, $103 billion growth plan in 2026 that it expects to grow further, targeting 20 gigawatts of new generation over the coming decade; the company said AI data center customers including Amazon, Microsoft, Google, and Meta were a primary driver alongside population growth of roughly 200,000 people a year into its service territory and grid-hardening investment against severe weather, per Fortune's reporting. Duke CEO Harry Sideris said hyperscale data center customers are paying for their own dedicated infrastructure and that broader rate increases stem mainly from population growth and grid resilience work rather than data centers alone; in Florida specifically, Duke has been replacing wooden utility poles with steel and concrete as part of its storm-hardening strategy. About 60% of Duke's planned capital spending is allocated to new generation (gas turbines, solar, battery storage, and nuclear plant life extensions) and the remaining 40% to grid expansion and upgrades. Duke separately confirmed in 2025 that it was exploring building data centers of its own in Florida, according to WUSF's reporting.

Florida's data center sales-tax landscape changed materially in 2025: House Bill 7031, effective August 1, 2025, eliminated the state's sales-tax exemption on equipment, electricity, and construction materials for data centers with IT loads below 100 megawatts, preserving the exemption only for facilities at or above that threshold, with no grandfather clause for existing sub-100 MW facilities, per Ryan LLC's tax-advisory analysis. All of Flexential's Florida buildings, including this one, operate well under that 100 MW threshold, meaning they and their colocation tenants would no longer qualify for the exemption on new purchases made after the effective date, a shift that has been reported to create potential retroactive tax exposure and pressure toward lease renegotiations for smaller colocation operators statewide.

reading.body:
Flexential Tampa North publishes 3.0 MW of critical load UPS capacity across 60,166 square feet, representing roughly 32 percent of Florida's disclosed data center power in operator specifications.

The facility holds compliance certifications for healthcare and payment processing, not AI-specific workloads. This matters because regulated industries occupy prime real estate and power in regional grids, and their continued claims on capacity constrain what remains available for compute-intensive applications. Tampa's four disclosed facilities total 9.35 MW. The remaining nine mapped facilities in Florida publish no power figures, so this picture is incomplete. Whether Flexential plans to redirect this facility toward AI, or has already done so under existing certifications, cannot be determined from published operator data.

The 3.0 MW figure states UPS capacity, not current IT load or allocated rack density. At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, it could support roughly 75 racks, but operator specs do not confirm compute is actually present or planned at that scale. Grid and power expansion constraints for this location are not public.
